question.text: Which of the following is the MOST commonly adopted legal form for domestic Cat I/II AIFs in India?

answer.text: Trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008
Private limited company under the Companies Act, 2013
Section 8 company under the Companies Act, 2013

explanation.text: The Logic: The majority of AIFs registered in India use the Trust form because of operational flexibility, lower compliance cost, confidentiality of investor identities, and freedom to draft bespoke governance in the trust deed. LLP is popular globally but less so in India. Sec 8 company is extremely rare. The Trap: LLP is the global (US/Cayman) norm but not the Indian norm. Private company adds cumbersome Companies Act compliance. Section 8 is not-for-profit and not practical for a commercial AIF. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests from distributor angle (which structure you sell). XIX-D asks from Manager angle (which structure is easiest to run). Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II trust-form AIFs should be drafted as 'irrevocable determinate' to preserve Section 115UB pass-through; LLP form loses the trust secrecy under the Trusts Act.
